AppCodeOut.description:
The answer to opening an emailed link that an installed app asked for: not a session in the
browser it was opened in, but a one-time code for the app.
AppCodeOut.title: AppCodeOut

AppExchangeIn.description: An installed app swapping its one-time code (and the secret it made) for a session.
AppExchangeIn.title: AppExchangeIn

BillingOut.description: How many sessions the person can start, and how far along their invite reward is.
BillingOut.title: BillingOut

BriefFactEdit.description: One change to the brief. No id adds a fact; an id updates, pins or removes (delete) it.
BriefFactEdit.title: BriefFactEdit

NotesIn.description:
A field left out is left as it is. The web app sends only the role; the text comes from the
CV upload.
NotesIn.title: NotesIn

OnboardingIn.description:
Finish onboarding with all four answers, or skip it. `role` is the CV page's target role;
`full_name` is only asked for when the account has none.
OnboardingIn.title: OnboardingIn

ProfileIn.description:
What a person can change about themselves. Only fields that are sent are changed; an empty
string clears an optional one.
ProfileIn.title: ProfileIn

StartupSentOut.description: A pitch sent to a startup, shown beside the job applications in one activity list.
StartupSentOut.title: StartupSentOut

UiRelease.description: A new copy of the interface the phone app can fetch and switch to without a new install.
UiRelease.title: UiRelease

avg_cost_per_research_job_usd.title: Avg Cost Per Research Job Usd

Utm.description: Campaign tags on the link someone arrived on (utm_source and friends).
Utm.title: Utm

delete.description:
Delete the user and everything they own at once. Backups age out within 30 days. One
confirmation email goes out afterwards, and the address is kept for nothing else.

put.description:
Change the password, or set a first one if the person only used email links or Google.
Changing it needs the current password, every other device is signed out, and an email tells
the account owner.

get.description: The log of everything happening on the platform, newest first.
The same log as a spreadsheet (up to 5,000 rows). Exporting is itself logged.

post.description:
Email a single-use back-office link, but only to staff. The answer is the same for every
address, so it cannot be used to find out who is on the staff list.

Exchange the emailed token for a staff cookie. POST, so a mail scanner that opens the link
cannot use the token up.

put.description:
Turn a kill switch on or off. Takes effect on the next claim, without a deploy; attempts
already sent are still settled.

get.description: Which emails went out and whether the provider took them. Never the body of a message.

schema.title: Response Email Templates Api Admin Emails Templates Get

get.description: A template filled with obviously fake data, to look at before it goes to anyone.
The boards jobs are read from, once for everyone: how many, how healthy, which fail.
The same list as a spreadsheet. Exporting is itself logged.
Every board and feed, the busiest first.
Where sign-ups come from and how far each channel gets, plus the signals for pricing.
Product health at a glance: growth, activity, the funnel, and what is going wrong.
How good and how fast the product is: ratings, speed, scores, and failures.

post.description: A held sign-up turned out to be a real, different person (say, a housemate): count it.

get.description: Everyone who asked (waiting first) or has startup outreach; `q` finds anyone by email.

put.description: Switch startup outreach on for one person, or off again (their pitches stop at once).

schema.title: Response Import Startups Api Admin Startups Import Post

get.description:
The startups behind the totals: name, website, who listed it, what it does, its contacts and
open roles. Filter by what the tiles count, a region, a directory, or a search.

schema.title: Response Run Research Api Admin Startups Research Post

get.description: Every open role found on the startups' own sites, with the startup and where to apply.

The owner's cost view: spend per day, the heaviest users, and the average cost of a session
and of a research job. These are ESTIMATES from counted audio seconds and tokens times the
PRICE_* settings; the provider's own billing is the source of truth.

One account: who they are, what they have done, and their activity. No CV text, transcripts
or answers: an admin sees what is happening, not what anyone said.

post.description:
Give someone free interviews, for support or goodwill. Logged against the admin, and the
person is told by email unless `notify` is off.

get.description:
The background queue: what is waiting, how long the oldest has waited, what gave up, and
how much worker time each kind of task used in the last day (its share of the cost).

post.description: Give a dead task a fresh set of attempts.

schema.title: Response Worker Retry Api Admin Worker Tasks  Task Id  Retry Post

get.description: The newest downloadable version of each app. Public: the same list as the releases page.

post.description:
An installed app swaps the one-time code from the system browser, plus the secret it made
before leaving, for its own session. The code alone is worthless.

get.description:
Google sends the browser here. Whatever happens, the browser lands back on the web app, and
the state cookie is used once.
Which sign-in methods the web app should offer.

post.description:
Email a single-use sign-in link to someone who has an account. An address with no account is
told so, plainly, and pointed to sign-up: no link is sent and nothing is created. (This does say
which addresses are registered; the per-address and per-client limits bound how fast it can be
asked.)
Email a password-reset link. Same answer for every address.
Choose a new password with the emailed link. Every other session is signed out.

Start an account with an email and password. Nothing takes effect until the emailed link is
opened, which proves the address. The answer is the same whether or not the email already has
an account; an existing account just gets an ordinary sign-in link.

Exchange the emailed token for a session cookie. POST (not GET) so a mail scanner that
prefetches the link cannot burn the token. If an installed app asked for the link, the browser
is not signed in: the app is handed a one-time code instead (see /auth/app-exchange).

schema.title: Response Verify Api Auth Verify Post
Response List Answers Api Autoapply Answers Get

post.description: Answer the question the application is waiting on, then prepare it again.
The candidate has looked at a criterion the listing did not settle and says to go ahead.
Name a hiring contact for this role. One note per role, under its own daily limit.
The candidate says what really happened to an application we could not confirm.
Check an application again, including one the candidate skipped earlier.

get.description: What the person is agreeing to, and what is still missing, shown before they switch on.
Next interview, what needs the candidate, and recent applications, in that order.

schema.title: Response Last Run Api Autoapply Discovery Last Get

post.description: Run today's search now. If it already ran today, nothing changes and that run is returned.

schema.title: Response Run Discovery Api Autoapply Discovery Run Post
Response Read Facts Api Autoapply Facts Get

post.description: Read the CV into a draft for the person to check. Nothing is confirmed by this call.

schema.title: Response List Interviews Api Autoapply Interviews Get

post.description:
Open this interview in the preparation part of the app: its company is created (or found)
and researched, and the session starts with the submitted CV and application.
A job address pasted by the candidate goes through the same checks as a discovered one.

get.description:
Google sends the browser back here. The state must match the cookie set when this person
started, and that cookie must name this very account.

post.description:
Log in to the connected mailbox again to confirm it still works (nothing is sent). A password
the provider no longer accepts moves the connection to 'reconnect needed'.
Gmail: returns the Google address to approve access at. Fixture mode connects at once.

Connect Gmail, Outlook or Yahoo with an app password. We log in once to check it (nothing is
sent), then keep it encrypted. It is never logged and never returned.
Stop sends and reads, revoke access, delete the credential. Other channels stay on.

schema.title: Response List Outreach Api Autoapply Outreach Get
Response List Recruiting Api Autoapply Recruiting Get

post.description: The message named no clear time zone, so the candidate says which one it was written in.
Settle an ambiguous employer message by choosing the application it belongs to.
Turn an earned invite reward into a free session the person can use.

schema.title: Response List Companies Api Companies Get

post.description: Save a company and start its research job.

put.description:
Edit company details. This does not start research by itself (it costs money); the page
offers "Research again" so the user decides.

Edit fact text, pin facts, add the user's own facts or delete facts. Only the changed facts
are sent. Edits and pins survive a refresh.

post.description:
Re-run research (bypasses the page cache). One job per company at a time: if one is
already running, its id is returned and nothing new starts.
Add text the app could not read itself. It is labelled "Pasted by you" in the brief.
Ask to be let in. Asking again changes nothing.

get.description:
How many startups outreach can write to, so the page can say so truthfully. Open to anyone
signed in, invited or not.

schema.title: Response Summary Api Hunt Summary Get
Response Targets Api Hunt Targets Get

delete.description: Remove the CV text. The target role stays.

post.description:
Upload a CV as the raw request body (PDF, Word .docx or text), with its name in the
`x-filename` header. Only the text it holds is kept, never the file. Replaces any earlier CV.

put.description:
Finish onboarding with all four answers, or skip it. Either way the person is not asked
again. The target role, if given, goes to the CV page.

get.description: Past sessions, newest first, with cursor pagination.

post.description:
Start an interview session. The person agreed at sign-up that their partner knows the
assistant is on; every account has that on record, and the session stores when. An account
without it cannot start a session.

delete.description: Delete one session with its transcript, outlines and scores. It leaves the app at once.

schema.title: Response Delete Session Api Sessions  Session Id  Delete

post.description: A fresh single-use token, for a reconnect or a second audio source (the microphone).

get.description: Retrieve or generate a 6-digit sync PIN for the desktop stealth overlay.

schema.title: Response Get Session Pin Api Sessions  Session Id  Pin Get

post.description: Score the user's answers after the session. Poll GET /sessions/{id} for the result.

When live streaming keeps failing, the browser cuts speech into segments and sends each
one here. Audio is transcribed and discarded; only the text is saved, as with a caption.

Stream an answer outline as server-sent events: delta, skip, done or error. If the client
disconnects, the stream (and the model call under it) is cancelled. A Standard Interview has
no real-time answers: transcript, notes and feedback only.
Send a test prompt/outline to any connected desktop stealth HUDs.

schema.title: Response Test Desktop Stream Api Sessions  Session Id  Test Desktop Post

get.description: The saved transcript as text, with timestamps (FR-34).

post.description: Thumbs up or down on an outline, stored with the session.

schema.title: Response Suggestion Feedback Api Suggestions  Suggestion Id  Feedback Post

put.description:
Remember that the first-time tour was finished or skipped, so it is not shown again. Asking
for done=false shows it again the next time the dashboard opens.

get.description: Liveness: the process is up.
Readiness: database reachable and provider key present.
